---
title: "tidyr"
---

The tidyr verbs use tidyr's argument names. Arguments that start with a dot in
tidyr start with an underscore here.

## Pivoting

`pivot_longer()` turns columns into rows of names and values. `names_prefix`
strips a regular expression from the start of each name. `names_sep` or
`names_pattern` split names into several `names_to` columns, and the special
name `'.value'` takes the value column's name from that part.
`values_drop_na: true` drops rows whose values are all NA.

`pivot_wider()` spreads names and values into columns. `id_cols` identify the
rows (by default every other column). `values_fill` fills missing cells,
`values_fn` combines duplicate cells, and `names_prefix`, `names_sep`,
`names_glue`, and `names_sort` control the new names. Without `values_fn`,
duplicate cells turn the value column into list-columns and raise tidyr's
warning.

Both verbs build tidyr's pivot spec in phplyr and pass it to the table's
`pivotLongerSpec()` or `pivotWiderSpec()`, so a backend can run the pivot
natively.

{{< include ../examples/_pivot.md >}}

## Missing combinations and values

`complete()` adds missing combinations of the given columns and fills other
columns with NA, or with values from `fill:`. A column name expands to its
unique values (a factor to its levels), `nesting()` keeps only combinations
that occur, and a named list supplies the values. It works within groups.
`expand()` returns only the combinations, and `crossing()` and `expand_grid()`
build a new table from lists.

{{< include ../examples/_complete.md >}}

`fill()` carries values down or up over NA within groups
(`_direction: 'down' | 'up' | 'downup' | 'updown'`). `drop_na()` drops rows
with NA in the given columns, and `replace_na()` replaces NA per column.

{{< include ../examples/_fill.md >}}

## Splitting and combining

| Function | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `separate_wider_delim(col, delim, names:)` | Split on a fixed string into columns |
| `separate_wider_position(col, widths)` | Split by character widths |
| `separate_wider_regex(col, patterns)` | Split with named regular expressions |
| `separate_longer_delim(col, delim)` | Split into rows |
| `separate_longer_position(col, width)` | Split into rows of fixed width |
| `separate(col, into, sep:)` | The superseded splitter, with `extra`, `fill`, and `convert` |
| `unite(col, ...cols, sep:)` | Paste columns together |
| `uncount('n', _id:)` | Repeat rows by a weight column |
| `nest(data: [...])`, `unnest('data')` | List-columns of tables |

`too_few` and `too_many` handle pieces that don't fit, as in tidyr.
